model.name: Atlas Enterprise Architecture
model.documentation: An ArchiMate 3.2 layered view of the Atlas BPMN workflow engine: motivation, business, application, technology, and implementation & deployment. Generated from gen_open_exchange.py; a communication and round-trip artifact, subordinate to the code and the deep-dives (see ADR-0099 and docs/architecture/enterprise-architecture.md).

element.name: Enterprise Architect
element.documentation: Owns capability fit, governance, and the invariants.

element.name: Process Modeler
element.documentation: Needs models to be authorable and readable, then executable.

element.name: Business / Task User
element.documentation: Needs human tasks to be reliable and never silently lost.

element.name: Operations
element.documentation: Needs to observe, audit, and recover long-running instances.

element.name: Integration Developer
element.documentation: Needs a stable protocol to attach external work (job workers).

element.name: Maintainer / AI Agent
element.documentation: Needs a codebase whose correctness rules are explicit.

element.name: Throughput pressure
element.documentation: Many instances per second per partition is a first-class goal.

element.name: Durability
element.documentation: A workflow engine that drops a token is worse than useless.

element.name: Long-running processes
element.documentation: Timers, message waits, and multi-week instances must survive restarts.

element.name: Operational robustness
element.documentation: Transient failures must pause, not crash, an instance.

element.name: Standard conformance
element.documentation: Full BPMN 2.0 execution semantics, not a subset dialect.

element.name: Contributor productivity
element.documentation: Humans and AI agents must change the engine safely.

element.name: Runtime XML interpretation is a throughput killer
element.documentation: Most BPMN engines interpret XML at runtime and write state to SQL one transaction at a time — both are throughput killers.

element.name: One fsync per event caps throughput
element.documentation: One fsync per event caps you at a few thousand events per second.

element.name: In-place state mutation invites consistency bugs
element.documentation: Did the DB write and the in-memory change both succeed? An entire class of consistency bugs that in-place mutation invites.

element.name: Durable execution of long-lived processes
element.documentation: Survive crashes and run long-lived processes.

element.name: Full BPMN 2.0 coverage
element.documentation: Subprocesses, boundary events, event subprocesses.

element.name: High throughput per partition
element.documentation: Many instances per second per partition.

element.name: Pure Go, no CGO, embedded state store
Throughput scales with batch size
element.documentation: Throughput scales with batch size, not with disk round-trips.

element.name: Recovery is a deterministic log replay
element.documentation: Single-writer plus event sourcing makes recovery a trivial fold.

element.name: Compile, don't interpret
element.documentation: Expensive work happens once at deploy, never on the hot path.

element.name: Event sourcing over state mutation
element.documentation: The log is the single source of truth; state is a fold of it.

element.name: Group commit for durability
element.documentation: Make many events durable with a single fsync.

element.name: Single writer per partition
element.documentation: One goroutine owns a partition's state; scale by adding partitions.

element.name: Invariant 1: no allocation on the hot path
Invariant 2: durable before visible
element.documentation: Append, one fsync, commit, then side effects.

element.name: Invariant 3: single writer per partition
element.documentation: Cross-partition work is async messaging only.

element.name: Invariant 4: one applyToState, live and on recovery
Invariant 5: compile, don't interpret
element.documentation: No parse/validate/compile on the hot path.

element.name: Invariant 6: events are facts, commands are intentions
element.documentation: Only events persist.
